question: Which of the activity deficits in the following enzymes of the urea cycle can cause an orotic aciduria, in addition to hyperammonemia ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase -> decreased urea cycle activity -> increased carbamoyl phosphate levels -> orotic aciduria and hyperammonemia -> 80% CHAIN: Ornithine transcarbamylase -> impaired urea cycle function -> accumulation of carbamoyl phosphate -> orotic aciduria and hyperammonemia -> 80%
analysis: Orotic aciduria is a rare metabolic disorder characterized by the excessive excretion of orotic acid in the urine. Deficiency in the enzyme carbamoyl phosphate synthetase can lead to orotic aciduria, in addition to hyperammonemia, as it is a key enzyme in the urea cycle responsible for the conversion of ammonia to urea.
